General stochastic optimisation · source-based formal development

PBGSO proof details and complete catalog

General optimiser responses and augmented sampler diffusions, with explicit analytic assumptions, proved comparison arguments and new bounds for the two implementation maps.

Source: Jiechen Jackie Zhang and O. Deniz Akyildiz, Particle-based Generalised Stochastic Optimisation, local manuscript. This page does not assign a publication venue or claim a published proof PDF.

Formal scope. The general model, actual Brownian/Itô integration, original stationary product laws, both source law-contraction branches, sharp original particle/parameter bounds, four appendix results and both actual particle-method bounds are proved. A2 means a stationary weak frozen SDE realization, not generator-only stationarity. A1 supplies full-system strong existence and same-driver uniqueness; actual path-space transport proves source stationarity across original probability spaces. No ambient measure separability is required. The constant-diffusion contraction uses the explicitly named ordinary finite signed-work reading of universal A3; an extended-negative-work theorem is not claimed. All eight numbered source statements and both actual method bounds are verified under these source interpretations. This finite-work convention is substantive and independent of the conditional joint inequality. Source A4/A5 derive target-comparison work without that convention. Both additive M-MFPO and HOL numerical endpoints construct their processes, Gaussian coupling, integral references and mesh-uniform constants. Primitive global joint Lipschitz force bounds for the methods, source A3, actual frozen invariance, P2\mathcal P_2P2​ laws and reference variance remain visible. The exact eight-result/two-method completion ledger below controls the strict verification result.

General framework

Let S,Θ,Z,XS,\Theta,Z,XS,Θ,Z,X be independent optimiser, parameter, sampler and observed-state spaces. A finite noise index describes the columns of σθ(z)\sigma_\theta(z)σθ​(z). Projections Pθ:S→ΘP_\theta:S\to\ThetaPθ​:S→Θ and Px:Z→XP_x:Z\to XPx​:Z→X, an observation F:Θ×X→ΘF:\Theta\times X\to\ThetaF:Θ×X→Θ, an arbitrary optimiser response Ψt\Psi_tΨt​, and sampler coefficients b,σb,\sigmab,σ define

Gν(s)=∫F(Pθs,Pxz) ν(dz),s˙t=Ψt(st,Gνt(st)),dZt=bPθst(Zt)dt+σPθst(Zt)dBt.G_\nu(s)=\int F(P_\theta s,P_xz)\,\nu(dz),\qquad \dot s_t=\Psi_t(s_t,G_{\nu_t}(s_t)),\qquad dZ_t=b_{P_\theta s_t}(Z_t)dt+\sigma_{P_\theta s_t}(Z_t)dB_t.Gν​(s)=∫F(Pθ​s,Px​z)ν(dz),s˙t​=Ψt​(st​,Gνt​​(st​)),dZt​=bPθ​st​​(Zt​)dt+σPθ​st​​(Zt​)dBt​.

The finite system uses GνN(s)=N−1∑iF(Pθs,PxZi)G_{\nu^N}(s)=N^{-1}\sum_iF(P_\theta s,P_xZ^i)GνN​(s)=N−1∑i​F(Pθ​s,Px​Zi), with N>0N>0N>0. The equality with the empirical-law integral is proved. Auxiliary optimiser variables and augmented sampler states are allowed; a common joint potential and equal parameter/sampler dimensions are unnecessary. The displayed optimiser equation has deterministic evolution; noisy-parameter IPLA requires an additional extension.

Source hypotheses and actual formal premises

The source convergence results require all of the following conditions where indicated; they are not implied merely by choosing a sampler with the correct invariant distribution.

  1. A1: well-posedness. Pathwise unique global finite-horizon mean-field strong solutions for deterministic optimiser initial states and sampler laws in P2\mathcal P_2P2​, preservation of second moments, and either constant diffusion or the stated linear growth bound. A finite-particle solution must also exist for results concerning that system.
  2. A2: stationary pair. Frozen invariance means an actual stationary weak frozen SDE realization on some probability space, retaining the complete sampler state; generator-only stationarity is insufficient. A critical point ∇ℓ(θ⋆)=0\nabla\ell(\theta_\star)=0∇ℓ(θ⋆​)=0, an augmented state s⋆s_\stars⋆​ with Pθs⋆=θ⋆P_\theta s_\star=\theta_\starPθ​s⋆​=θ⋆​, Ψt(s⋆,0)=0\Psi_t(s_\star,0)=0Ψt​(s⋆​,0)=0 for every nonnegative time, and a finite-second-moment frozen invariant sampler law with the required marginal. Despite its source label, this does not say global minimiser.
  3. A3: joint twisted contractivity. Positive definite optimiser and sampler quadratic weights give, for every pair of states, every two admissible laws and every coupling, the joint drift pairing plus half the squared weighted diffusion difference at most −ρ-\rho−ρ times the joint squared energy, with ρ>0\rho>0ρ>0.
  4. A4: gradient response. Ψt(s,⋅)\Psi_t(s,\cdot)Ψt​(s,⋅) is uniformly LΨL_\PsiLΨ​-Lipschitz.
  5. A5: uniform fluctuations. Along the chosen mean-field path, sup⁡tE∥F(θˉt,PxZˉt)−Gνˉt(sˉt)∥2≤VF<∞\sup_t\mathbb E\|F(\bar\theta_t,P_x\bar Z_t)-G_{\bar\nu_t}(\bar s_t)\|^2\le V_F<\inftysupt​E∥F(θˉt​,Px​Zˉt​)−Gνˉt​​(sˉt​)∥2≤VF​<∞.
  6. Probability and integrability. Positive particle count, deterministic optimiser initial state, i.i.d. sampler initial states independent of independent Brownian drivers, synchronous paired coupling, and the actual observation/test domains stated in each theorem. Energy identities, localization moments and noise properties are derived by the actual-process results where claimed. Background integrability only under πθ\pi_\thetaπθ​ does not establish observation domains for arbitrary comparison laws.

Finite signed-integral convention for A3. The low-level joint inequality is tested on couplings where its integrals exist. Separately, FiniteCouplingWork states that the signed sampler work is absolutely integrable for every joint probability law of finite quadratic moment, for every optimiser pair. This is the explicit ordinary finite-integral reading of the source’s universal A3 formula. The constant-diffusion source2 development uses this property; it is not inferred from the conditional inequality.

The convention is substantive. Lean constructs a P2\mathcal P_2P2​ law for which the strongly dissipative scalar drift b(z)=−z−z3b(z)=-z-z^3b(z)=−z−z3 has nonintegrable signed work against zero. An extended-negative-work reading therefore covers more superlinear models. The projected criteria establish the joint inequality on their displayed integrability domains; they do not automatically certify universal finite work. A finite reading of the universal U5 signed integrals must likewise be stated explicitly when combining that criterion with the constant-diffusion law theorem.

Every supporting module below has a scope and assumption note. The exact assumption inventory contains every current theorem header, full structure/definition contract and shared module context. The Lean panels are read from source at build time.

Source continuous-time bounds

Writing d2=∥s−s~∥2+W22(ν,ν~)d^2=\|s-\widetilde s\|^2+W_2^2(\nu,\widetilde\nu)d2=∥s−s∥2+W22​(ν,ν) and κ\kappaκ for the ratio of upper and lower metric eigenvalue bounds, the source establishes

dt≤κe−ρtd0,∥θtN−θ⋆∥L2≤κe−ρtd0+LΨρκVFN(1−e−ρt).d_t\le\sqrt\kappa e^{-\rho t}d_0,\qquad \|\theta_t^N-\theta_\star\|_{L^2}\le\sqrt\kappa e^{-\rho t}d_0+ \frac{L_\Psi}{\rho}\sqrt{\frac{\kappa V_F}{N}}(1-e^{-\rho t}).dt​≤κ​e−ρtd0​,∥θtN​−θ⋆​∥L2​≤κ​e−ρtd0​+ρLΨ​​NκVF​​​(1−e−ρt).

Its interaction estimate compares interacting particles with an independent-copy empirical law, not directly with the population law. A full empirical Wasserstein error needs an additional sampling term. Stationary uniqueness is restricted to finite-second-moment laws δs⊗ν\delta_s\otimes\nuδs​⊗ν. None of the source's continuous-time theorems establishes a method-specific time discretisation rate.

What the formal statements prove

Source stationary product law from weak frozen invariance and A1

A2 has its SDE meaning. There is an actual stationary weak frozen sampler on some Brownian probability space, with its original locally constructed stochastic equation, continuous adapted paths, pathwise Bochner-L1L^1L1 drift and invariant P2\mathcal P_2P2​ output law. A generator-only invariant test identity does not supply this assumption. The frozen process need not be strong or live on the original solution’s source.

A1 supplies the full coupled solution. Use its direct strong-existence instance on independent initial sampler law times the actual Wiener path law, and same-driver pathwise uniqueness on the proved valid Brownian filtrations. The initial/Wiener-path map, whole-path Gaussian laws, initialization independence, causal filtration transport and original local-noise naturality are all derived. Pulling this full-system solution to the frozen and original sources and applying uniqueness proves the literal stationary product law on the original source.

Zero mean observation, its integrability, the optimiser fixed point at every horizon time, the stationary initial sampler law and matching deterministic optimiser initial value remain explicit. The optimiser satisfies its original integral ODE. No growth, global drift moment, energy estimate, common-source frozen strong realization or final output-law equality is supplied.

Complete proof and source context

Original linear-growth strong equations derive moments and true-law contraction

The original simultaneous raw equation is driven by the actually constructed local Brownian integral. Its initial variable is L2L^2L2, and primitive linear growth bounds the drift plus the Euclidean column norm by K(1+P+∥Xt∥)K(1+P+\|X_t\|)K(1+P+∥Xt​∥), with K,P≥0K,P\ge0K,P≥0. The local energy controls raw drift variation and diffusion squares; genuine first-hit stops and capped computed martingales derive the stopped equations and all stopped moments.

Actual stochastic isometry and a Volterra argument yield a bound independent of the stopping threshold. Fatou then gives, for every t≤Tt\le Tt≤T,

E∥Xt∥2≤BT,E0=E∥X0∥2,A=1+P2,cT=9K2(T+1)T,BT=ecT(3E0+A)−A.\begin{gathered}\mathbb E\|X_t\|^2\le B_T,\\E_0=\mathbb E\|X_0\|^2,\\A=1+P^2,\\c_T=9K^2(T+1)T,\\B_T=e^{c_T}(3E_0+A)-A.\end{gathered}E∥Xt​∥2≤BT​,E0​=E∥X0​∥2,A=1+P2,cT​=9K2(T+1)T,BT​=ecT​(3E0​+A)−A.​

The original optimiser integral equation and continuous parameter projection derive a finite PPP on each horizon. Primitive growth and BTB_TBT​ then give actual spatial and product-time L2L^2L2 drift/diffusion. Genuine stopped-integral consistency proves that the original local noise equals the original global computed integral; every predictable Model datum and its literal sampler-law identity are constructed.

Actual path-space law uniqueness transfers canonical contraction to the original raw solutions on distinct probability spaces. Source A3 therefore proves the exact κe−ρT\sqrt\kappa e^{-\rho T}κ​e−ρT contraction with the true optimal initial Wasserstein distance. No global moment, L2L^2L2 coefficient curve, noise-matching, output-law or all-couplings-realization premise remains. Original coefficient measurability and model realization, observation domains, original optimiser equation and P2\mathcal P_2P2​ initial laws remain explicit. The superlinear constant-diffusion A1(i) branch does not follow from this growth proof.

/-- The original local path-energy cap bounds actual stopped drift variation. -/

/-- Local stopped states have actual spatial L² values, derived from their
original raw equations and true capped Brownian martingales. -/

/-- Genuine martingale endpoint moments are bounded by their terminal
moment; the actual stopped diffusion cap then supplies the numerical bound. -/

/-- Localized raw state moments follow from the literal capped variation
and actual constructed noise, without any original state-moment premise. -/

/-- All finite physical columns are represented in their literal Euclidean
noise norm; the full primitive growth inequality retains every column. -/


/-- Primitive raw linear growth applies to the actual stopped state. Both
spatial coefficient moments are conclusions of this theorem. -/


/-- The local state bound derives genuine stopped drift product L², even
though the original raw drift was assumed only pathwise L¹. -/

/-- Literal actual stopped-state L² coordinate. -/






/-- Original raw stopped equations produce the actual integral equation in
L²; all raw/curve identities and drift Fubini transfer are derived. -/

/-- The literal initial stopped state is the actual original initial class. -/

/-- The actual finite-column L² curve has exactly the original packed
spatial L² norm. This identity is proved from literal finite coordinates. -/

/-- Primitive pointwise linear growth gives the actual stopped-curve
quadratic coefficient inequality needed by deterministic Volterra comparison. -/

/-- Explicit global moment budget independent of the localization index. -/

/-- The actual localized process obeys a horizon-uniform moment bound with
no localization-dependent constant. All stochastic identities are derived. -/


/-- The original raw state has its actual global second moment by Fatou
from the constructed horizon-exhausting stopped processes. -/





/-- Spatial moments of the full original coefficients follow at every time,
including time zero; exceptional non-L² sections are not silently discarded. -/

/-- The original drift and all finite physical diffusion columns have actual
global expected time-square integrability. This is a conclusion of primitive
linear growth and the original local strong equation. -/

/-- The local integral in the original equation is the actual global raw
computed Brownian integral after linear-growth moment transfer. Equality is
derived by genuine stopped-integral identities and horizon exhaustion. -/

/-- The original raw state equation is now realized by the actual global
computed integral; no global-noise or L²-coordinate compatibility is assumed. -/

end Data
end PBGSO.RawLinearGrowthState

Primitive original local equations and linear growth derive all global
coefficient moments and the literal constructed predictable model data.

full-probability event; no stochastic, law or energy conclusion is supplied.
-/

variable {Ω I Z S Θ X : Type*} [mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]

/-- A single full-probability coefficient realization yields genuine
product-a.e. coefficient equality on the finite horizon. -/

this structure are conclusions of `RawLinearGrowthState.Data`, not inputs. -/

namespace Realization

/-- Global product square moments of the original MODEL coefficients are
transferred from the proved localized moment bounds. -/



/-- The original local strong equation is the original MODEL's global
computed integral equation. Both the noise transfer and drift identity are
proved; neither is an interface hypothesis. -/

/-- Actual predictable Model data are constructed from primitive original
local strong equations and linear growth. Global state/coefficient moments,
noise matching, L² section identities and the sampler equation are derived. -/

/-- The constructed sampler law is exactly the original raw sampler law. -/

end Realization
end PBGSO.RawLinearGrowthModel

import PBGSO.RawSolutionLawUniqueness

/-! # Linear-growth contraction on arbitrary original probability spaces
Original solution laws are identified with actual canonical Gaussian-source
strong solutions through one genuine Wiener-path-source solution per initial
law. These are direct strong-well-posedness instances; no output-law match or
common frozen realization is assumed. The canonical equations satisfy the
explicit primitive linear-growth realization regularity.
-/

set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set Filter
open scoped NNReal ENNReal Topology

variable {Ω Ω' S Θ Z X I : Type*}
  [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace Ω'] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]

  [NormedAddCommGroup Θ] [NormedSpace ℝ Θ] [CompleteSpace Θ]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Z] [InnerProductSpace ℝ Z] [CompleteSpace Z]
  [MeasurableSpace Z] [BorelSpace Z] [SecondCountableTopology Z]
  {Q : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]
  {R : Measure Ω'} [IsProbabilityMeasure R]
  {D : Driver (I := I) Q} {E : Driver (I := I) R}
  {M : Model S Θ Z X I} {T : ℝ≥0}

/-- Actual canonical strong existence plus primitive linear-growth
regularity. The only identities are the original initial conditions. -/

/-- Source A3 law contraction for original raw solutions on two arbitrary
filtered Brownian sources. Strong well-posedness is used through actual
canonical/path-source existence and original-source pathwise uniqueness;
all marginal-law and stochastic matching conclusions are proved. -/

end PBGSO.RawSamplerGrowthArbitraryLaw

Source constant-diffusion law contraction: finite signed A3 integrals

Use finite-dimensional complete Borel second-countable optimiser and sampler coordinates, with finitely many Brownian columns. Original solutions on two arbitrary Brownian probability spaces satisfy their original local stochastic equations and optimiser integral ODE. The sampler drift is only pathwise Bochner L1L^1L1; no drift-norm growth or time-L1L^1L1(L2L^2L2) condition is imposed. Source A1 supplies its direct canonical and Wiener-path strong-existence instances plus same-driver uniqueness on the proved valid filtrations.

The signed-integral convention is a visible premise. In addition to the conditional joint inequality, assume FiniteCouplingWork: for every optimiser pair and every joint probability measure with finite quadratic moment, the signed sampler coupling work is absolutely integrable. This is the ordinary finite-integral reading of the universal formula in A3. It has no observation-domain restriction.

Complete proof and source context

Actual local integration and weak finite-variation quadratic calculus

Joint raw diffusion fields have actual spatial L2L^2L2 sections, constructed integration, continuous martingale versions, exact weighted energy and valid coupling transport. First-hit localization uses the literal progressive path-energy integral. A single common null regularization handles almost-sure local integrability, and the actual local noise is glued from computed stopped integrals with simultaneous stopped identities.

Separate finite-variation theorems derive expected quadratic balance from original continuous paths, only pathwise Bochner-L1L^1L1 drift, actual computed noise and a square-integrable random total-variation budget. Strong Doob and genuine primitives construct every maximal radius and L2L^2L2 auxiliary variable internally. Product drift-work integrability and the integral energy family at every earlier time are derived. No time-L1L^1L1(L2L^2L2) drift, martingale, stochastic-isometry, radius or final energy conclusion is supplied to these final computed statements.

The source results above use this actual calculus with derived local gauges and moments. The optional one-sided positive-work criterion remains available independently of the finite signed-integral convention; every theorem retains its actual domain explicitly.

/-! # A one-sided work criterion for the constant-diffusion branch
The paper's joint condition implies pointwise frozen-sampler dissipativity.
Only the parameter-cross drift can contribute uncontrolled positive work.
The resulting positive-work integrability criterion is strictly weaker than
square integrability of the full sampler drift or its total variation.

Physical coefficient identities and the simultaneous original local equation are explicit process assumptions. The energy, work integrability, stopped identities, diffusion isometry, empirical-statistic measurability and final bound are derived. There is no global drift L2L^2L2, linear-growth or weak-generator test-domain premise.

The inputs are a natural one-copy mean-field solution UUU and an actual original native empirical solution YYY on the independent whole-seed product probability space. YYY uses the literal finite-average response, the shared random optimiser and the original physical diffusion columns. Positive particle count, initial L2L^2L2 and synchronous original initial coordinates are explicit; mean-field A1 alone is not asserted to construct an arbitrary particle solution.

Visible process and target assumptions. An actual native empirical solution YYY on the independent whole-seed product, a natural mean-field solution UUU, P2\mathcal P_2P2​ initial/target laws, synchronous original initialization, primitive Borel fields, a one-Lipschitz parameter projection, positive N,ρN,\rhoN,ρ, A3/A4/A5 and an actual constant stationary target solution. Source A1 is used through its direct canonical/path strong-existence instances and same-driver uniqueness. The target stationarity is the original SDE assertion proved from A2 above, with zero mean observation and optimiser fixed point, rather than a generator-only condition.

The constant-diffusion branch derives target positive work from A4 and reference variance; it does not require universal FiniteCouplingWork. The state-dependent branch assumes the original primitive linear-growth/Borel/progressive regularity and derives global moments and stochastic realization. Every independent reference law, physical pair equation, original parameter identity, true initial infimum and L2L^2L2 triangle is proved. No paired process, iid interacting law, work/energy estimate, coefficient/noise matching or final rate is a premise. Supporting comparison and realization interfaces

The original source results above derive their actual stochastic calculus and process assembly. The following earlier interfaces retain their own equation, test-domain and integrability contracts; their module-specific conditions are not open obligations in the completed source ledger.

Weak stationarity from a frozen sampler

The constant candidate solves the explicit optimiser ODE and generator forward equation. Given uniqueness of that weak formulation, every solution with the same initial state and law is constant. Integrability, frozen generator stationarity, zero mean observation and the optimiser fixed point are explicit inputs.

/-!
# The general particle-based gradient stochastic optimisation framework

`Model` has independent optimiser, parameter, sampler, observation and noise
coordinate types. In particular neither the optimiser nor the sampler is
restricted to a first-order gradient flow. Auxiliary momenta and adaptive
optimiser variables belong to `S`; augmented sampler variables belong to `Z`.

`IsWeakSolution` states the actual optimiser ODE and weak Fokker--Planck
equation. It is a law-level solution notion. No existence, equivalence to a
strong SDE, or stochastic Itô formula is asserted by this file.
-/

empty particle population. -/

/-- The sampler empirical measure. At positive population size its total
mass is one; zero population is excluded by all sampling estimates. -/

/-- The finite-sum gradient is exactly integration against the empirical

/-- The empirical law is a probability law for positive particle count. -/

/-- The continuous-time particle vector field, before time discretisation. -/

/-- An Euler step for an arbitrary optimiser response and sampler. `noise`

/-- The frozen sampler generator, including state- and parameter-dependent
diffusion. The two Fréchet derivatives are evaluated in sampler coordinates. -/

/-- A weak law solution for a specified separating test family. This makes
the analytic solution notion explicit instead of assuming an error bound.
Integrability is required rather than relying on totalised integrals. -/

/-- Frozen stationarity stated at the infinitesimal generator level. This
is an analytic input: boundary conditions and generator-domain arguments
must establish it for a proposed Gibbs diffusion. -/

/-- Uniqueness is quantified over the explicit ODE/forward equation above.

/-- Paper Theorem 1 at the explicit weak-solution level. The only analytic

/-- The gradient identity makes every stationary point suitable for the

/-- Relabelling particles does not change their common gradient estimate. -/

end Model

Complete proof and source context

Stationary product law from actual integral equations

The sampler satisfies an actual pathwise drift-integral equation retaining arbitrary state- and parameter-dependent diffusion. A supplied frozen invariant trajectory, zero mean observation and optimiser fixed point construct the constant-optimiser candidate. Same-driver pathwise uniqueness then proves that the full output law is literally the Dirac optimiser tensor frozen sampler law.

The integral interpretation is explicit. The operator JJJ and admissible process class CCC are supplied by the implementation. Both the candidate and compared process satisfy CCC, and uniqueness is restricted to that same class; no Itô or adaptation implementation is constructed in this result. The hypotheses include the actual frozen trajectory and its constant output law, finite second moment, observation integrability, the optimiser fixed point at every nonnegative time, pathwise uniqueness for the displayed equations, and matching initial variables. The explicit class CCC can encode adaptedness, initial-noise independence and integrand admissibility; instantiating JJJ, CCC and their uniqueness from source A1 remains an obligation. These are equation-level stationarity proofs; their intended Itô/process interpretation remains separate.

Stationarity and same-initial uniqueness for the computed integral

The frozen sampler satisfies the original equation driven by the actually constructed predictable Brownian integral, with actual invariant output law. Zero mean observation and the optimiser fixed point construct the constant-optimiser model trajectory. Same-initial uniqueness proves its literal Dirac optimiser tensor sampler stationary law. Source A3 independently derives that uniqueness in this class, without requiring a positive contraction rate merely for uniqueness.

Exact scope. The sampler drift is Bochner L1L^1L1 in time with L2L^2L2 values, diffusion is adapted time-L2L^2L2, and observation integrability, measurable model coefficients and genuine Driver properties are explicit. No arbitrary stochastic operator or stochastic-energy conclusion is assumed. Source A2 supplies actual frozen invariance; it is not inferred from a formal density cancellation. The later raw linear-growth theorem derives this realization from original local equations in A1(ii); the alternative superlinear constant-diffusion contraction remains separate, while the later original local path-space theorem proves stationarity from actual weak frozen SDE invariance.

Stationary product law for the original locally integrable strong equation

The stochastic noise is the actual constructed local Brownian integral of the original finite diffusion columns. The sampler has continuous adapted paths and merely pathwise Bochner-L1L^1L1 drift; no time-L1L^1L1(L2L^2L2) drift, linear growth or expected-energy hypothesis is imposed. The optimiser obeys its original integral ODE with an integrable field, allowing time-measurable responses.

Source same-driver uniqueness, an actual frozen invariant sampler trajectory on that Driver, zero mean observation and the optimiser fixed point construct the constant candidate and prove the literal stationary product law. The frozen law’s normalization and P2\mathcal P_2P2​ follow from its actual initial L2L^2L2 variable.

Realization is explicit. The compared sampler and frozen sampler must have the same initial random variable almost surely. The common-Driver condition belongs to this intermediate theorem. The following actual Wiener-path transfer proves the source stationarity assertion from a stationary weak frozen sampler on another source and the direct A1 full-system strong-solution instance; a common-source frozen strong solver is unnecessary.

Full multiplicative weak-generator contraction and optimal law distance

The actual synchronous pair generator acts on the twisted quadratic separation test. Its diffusion term is the squared difference of the full state- and parameter-dependent diffusion columns. The weak forward equation and optimiser ODE derive the energy derivative; no final dissipation or transport bound is assumed.

Et≤e−2ρtE0,dt≤κe−ρtd0,d2=∥s−s′∥2+W22(ν,ν′).\begin{gathered}E_t\le e^{-2\rho t}E_0,\\d_t\le\sqrt\kappa e^{-\rho t}d_0,\\d^2=\|s-s^\prime\|^2+W_2^2(\nu,\nu^\prime).\end{gathered}Et​≤e−2ρtE0​,dt​≤κ​e−ρtd0​,d2=∥s−s′∥2+W22​(ν,ν′).​

Exact analytic premises. Supply actual marginal weak solutions, a synchronous pair forward equation, finite second moments, observation/test/generator integrability, and membership of the quadratic separation test in the generator domain. The law theorem requires such a synchronous realization with the same specified marginal trajectories for every genuine initial coupling. Arbitrarily approximating couplings prove the infimum bound; optimal-coupling attainment is unnecessary. The actual Euclidean product-law W2W_2W2​ is proved equal to the displayed component metric, using literal Dirac optimiser tensor sampler laws and lifted/projected measure couplings; that identity is not assumed. Positive ρ\rhoρ then proves equality of two stationary optimiser states and sampler laws. The additive construction below proves the required law-preserving realization for autonomous constant-diffusion dynamics and common continuous input on the quadratic domain. This intermediate generator theorem retains its specified domain and realizability inputs. The original raw-process results above derive actual stochastic realizations under their stated A1 alternatives; no richer marginal generator domain is needed for those proofs.

particular stochastic implementation.

import PBGSO.MeanFieldContraction

/-!
# From actual coupling energies to Wasserstein laws

The transport distance is the infimum over all genuine initial couplings.
No optimal-coupling existence or supplied Wasserstein conclusion is assumed.
The generic energy theorem takes actual output couplings and their quadratic
energy comparisons; coupled-generator or integral-equation arguments can
produce those data. Realising the same output laws from every initial coupling
is an explicit process-level requirement of that theorem.

The additive specialisation below applies to actual integral solutions of
the independent general observation/response/sampler maps. It derives the
sampler law bound from their proved common-input contraction. State-dependent
strong-SDE and martingale-problem equivalence are separate requirements.
-/

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set
open scoped NNReal ENNReal Topology
namespace PBGSO

section CouplingCost
variable {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H]
  [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H]

omit [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] in
/-- The genuine coupling cost squared is its quadratic integral, whenever
the difference has a finite second moment. -/

omit [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] in
/-- Finite-second-moment marginals make every coupling cost finite; this
does not require the coupling to be independent or optimal. -/

omit [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] in
/-- A finite actual joint law bounds the ordinary real-valued transport
distance without converting infinity to zero. -/

omit [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H]
  [SecondCountableTopology H] in
/-- The first norm moment is at most the root second moment on a probability
space. Applied to the actual coupling difference, this supplies the
characteristic-function estimate used for separation of transport laws. -/

/-- The characteristic functions of the two marginal laws are controlled by
the cost of any finite coupling. -/

/-- Pairing particle i with particle i gives the finite empirical
Wasserstein bound. The proof uses the genuine empirical pair measure and
computes its quadratic transport cost exactly; no particle independence is
assumed. The positive particle count makes the two empirical measures laws. -/

variable [CompleteSpace H]

/-- Zero quadratic transport separates probability laws. The proof chooses
arbitrarily small finite couplings from the defining infimum and compares
characteristic functions; no optimal coupling is assumed. -/

/-- The real transport distance can be used for equality only after its
finiteness has been established explicitly. -/

end CouplingCost

section InfimumBridge
variable {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H]
  [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H]

/-- Actual quadratic coupling energies give the condition-number prefactor
after taking the infimum over all initial couplings. The family contains
output joint laws, not a supplied Wasserstein bound or an optimal coupling. -/

omit [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] in
/-- Finite couplings whose costs converge to the defining transport
infimum. Attainment of that infimum is unnecessary. -/

omit [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] in
/-- Any continuous bound in the actual initial coupling cost passes to the
optimal transport infimum. This also supports the mixed deterministic-law
quadratic metric, whose square root is not affine. -/

end InfimumBridge

section WeakLaws
variable {S Θ Z X I : Type*}
  [NormedAddCommGroup S] [InnerProductSpace ℝ S]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Θ] [NormedSpace ℝ Θ]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Z] [InnerProductSpace ℝ Z]
  [MeasurableSpace Z] [BorelSpace Z] [SecondCountableTopology Z] [Fintype I]

/-- The paper's Euclidean product distance between a deterministic full
optimiser state and a sampler law. Its transport component is a genuine
infimum over all couplings. Finiteness is proved in its use below. -/

/-- The full multiplicative-noise weak-generator contraction passes to the
optimal law distance. The process hypothesis is an actual synchronous weak
solution with the specified marginal trajectories for every initial coupling;
it is not an energy inequality or a Wasserstein-bound hypothesis. The
quadratic separation test must explicitly belong to the generator domain. -/

/-- Stationary uniqueness is a law equality, obtained by decay and the
separation property of the transport infimum. Existence of the stationary
weak laws and of their synchronous realizations remains explicit. -/

end WeakLaws

variable {Ω A Z G H : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]

  [NormedAddCommGroup Z] [NormedSpace ℝ Z] [CompleteSpace Z]

  [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H]
  (Q : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]
  (D : PBGSO.LipschitzDynamics A Z G)

/-- Constructed actual general additive integral solutions contract their
deterministic optimiser and sampler laws. The initial sampler cost here is
the selected L² coupling. Optimising that cost across law-preserving
realisations is performed separately by `bound_of_all_finite_couplings`.
The norm on the Banach product is the maximum norm, made explicit by `max`. -/

end LipschitzDynamics
end PBGSO

Complete proof and source context

Constructed integral solutions and actual drift contraction

For time-independent, globally Lipschitz observation, optimiser response and sampler drift maps, the code constructs actual finite-horizon integral solutions in a deterministic optimiser coordinate times an L2L^2L2 sampler coordinate. It also constructs an interacting-system L2L^2L2 solution using the actual finite average. A continuous additive sampler input is supplied; this does not construct a state-dependent Itô integral. The model definition and weak stationarity statements separately allow time-dependent optimiser responses.

For two continuous integral solutions with common additive input, a globally Lipschitz drift and a continuous linear transformation CCC into a Hilbert space, assume

ρ∥C(y−z)∥2≤⟨C(y−z),C(g(y)−g(z))⟩.\rho\|C(y-z)\|^2\le\langle C(y-z),C(g(y)-g(z))\rangle.ρ∥C(y−z)∥2≤⟨C(y−z),C(g(y)−g(z))⟩.

The derived difference equation proves ∥C(Yt−Zt)∥≤e−ρt∥C(Y0−Z0)∥\|C(Y_t-Z_t)\|\le e^{-\rho t}\|C(Y_0-Z_0)\|∥C(Yt​−Zt​)∥≤e−ρt∥C(Y0​−Z0​)∥, with the stated norm-comparison prefactor when converted back to the original norm. This theorem derives its energy derivative from the actual integral equations rather than assuming the final scalar differential inequality. A separate nonautonomous version allows time-dependent drift along supplied continuous integral solutions; it does not construct those solutions.

AdditiveJointBridge derives the lifted drift inequality directly from source A3 using the actual sampler-pair pushforward law, its marginals and weighted L2L^2L2 work identities. It then constructs both solutions and gives the exact Euclidean optimiser/L2L^2L2-sampler contraction. Its model compatibility requires the displayed independent observation/sampler maps, an autonomous optimiser response and constant diffusion columns. It does not assume the requested lifted dissipation bound. The common continuous input is arbitrary; identifying a particular Brownian input KKK with that Model also requires its diffusion columns to equal 2Kei\sqrt2Ke_i2​Kei​. AdditiveDiffusion constructs a normalized KKK from every finite constant diffusion family and proves this identity, together with the actual input scaling.

The Brownian-input module derives an L2L^2L2 square-root increment bound from given coordinate pre-Brownian laws and constructs mean-field integral solutions for any fixed linear diffusion map. Coordinate independence remains a separate hypothesis when needed for an SDE interpretation.

import ProximalLangevin.MeanFieldProcess

/-! # Actual additive-input mean-field dynamics for general forces

The optimiser is a deterministic Banach-space coordinate, the sampler an L²
random variable. Observation, optimiser response and sampler drift are separate
globally Lipschitz maps. No potential or equality of coordinate dimensions is
required. This constructs norm-continuous integral solutions; it does not
assert an almost-surely continuous strong SDE or a state-dependent Itô integral.
-/

/-! # From source law monotonicity to constructed additive integral processes

The joint sampler law is the pushforward of the actual L² pair on the common
probability space. Its marginals, expectations, weighted work and quadratic
cost are identified explicitly. Source joint monotonicity therefore yields the
lifted drift dissipation; that lifted inequality is not an assumption.
The optimiser response is autonomous in this subclass, and diffusion columns
are constant. No conservative potential or equality of force types is used.
-/

not supplied as a hypothesis. Shared additive noise cancels in those
equations. State-dependent stochastic noise requires a separate Itô proof.

Constructed global additive processes and actual quadratic weak realization

Primitive global Lipschitz maps and a continuous sampler input starting at zero construct a global norm-continuous optimiser/L2L^2L2-sampler integral process. Finite Picard solutions are glued using proved common-input uniqueness. Its actual optimiser ODE, pushforward sampler laws, finite second moments and observation integrability are derived. The synchronous pair quadratic forward equation follows from the actual common-input cancellation.

The generator domain is explicit. The constructed marginal test family is exactly empty and the pair test family is the singleton quadratic separation test. This is enough for the proved coupling-energy calculation; it does not assert the full marginal Itô/Fokker–Planck equation on arbitrary test functions. The model response is autonomous and diffusion columns constant. AdditiveDiffusion constructs the normalized finite-column diffusion map and proves its exact Brownian scaling, so no matrix-matching premise is needed for that constructed input. An arbitrary supplied input still needs its model interpretation. A measure-preserving L2L^2L2 pullback preserves the actual primitive field, integral solution and sampler law; no force or law equality is assumed in that change-of-space result.

Constructed additive laws contract over all initial couplings

Each actual global marginal trajectory is selected once on its initial-law times noise probability space. For every genuine initial coupling, the two measure-preserving projections pull those fixed processes to initial-coupling times noise space. Their output marginals are proved unchanged, their sampler inputs coincide, and the initial joint law is exactly the supplied coupling.

Source A3 and the derived quadratic forward equation therefore prove the optimal optimiser–Wasserstein contraction for the constructed law trajectories. There is no assumed output-law identity or all-couplings realization in the final theorem. Primitive maps are globally Lipschitz, the response autonomous, diffusion columns constant and the input common and continuous from zero. The marginal test domain remains empty and the pair domain the quadratic singleton; the model Brownian input can be constructed with exact coefficient matching, while adaptation, richer marginal Itô equations and frozen target invariance remain separate.

Actual frozen trajectories construct the additive stationary target

The frozen sampler input is an actual continuous L2L^2L2 trajectory with its original integral equation and constant output law, expressing the source frozen invariance assumption. Zero mean observation and the optimiser fixed point derive the complete constant-optimiser mean-field solution. Primitive common-input uniqueness proves that the canonical target process is stationary.

The all-initial-coupling construction then builds the full stationary-target data used by the parameter theorem; no target realizer, relaxation estimate or final output-law identity is assumed. Primitive Lipschitz maps, autonomous response, constant diffusion compatibility, positive source A3 and a one-Lipschitz parameter projection remain explicit. Marginal tests are empty, but actual frozen invariance is a substantive process input rather than a conclusion drawn from an empty test family.

Quadratic energy derived from an actual martingale residual

For a norm-continuous L2L^2L2 process, subtract its initial value and actual Bochner drift integral. If this residual has a standard martingale representative and the displayed weighted diffusion-increment isometry, conditional expectation proves orthogonality to the adapted earlier state. Exact quadratic increments and limiting remainders derive the expected energy derivative.

The state, drift and finite diffusion columns are norm-continuous, the state is adapted, and the metric weight is symmetric. No expected-energy derivative or weak forward equation is supplied. The weighted increment isometry is an explicit stochastic-integral property; constructing the intended multiplicative Itô integral and deriving its martingale/isometry hypotheses remain separate.

Complete proof and source context

Constructed vector Itô integration for time-L2L^2L2 adapted columns

Actual predictable Brownian sums derive the finite martingale and weighted isometry identities. Their literal time-L2L^2L2 embeddings complete on the closed range of all genuine adapted steps. Past translation averages, Fubini identification and continuous adapted approximants prove that every horizon time-L2L^2L2 column family with current-past AE measurability belongs to this domain, including every interval cut.

The computed integral has a standard adapted square-integrable martingale representative, exact weighted increment moments, zero initial value, actual L2L^2L2-time continuity, subtraction, and measure-preserving source/valid-filtration transport. No diffusion time continuity, supplied approximation, stochastic isometry or martingale conclusion is required.

Scope. These are actual constructed integrals for time-L2L^2L2 adapted columns. The general source A1 solution class still needs its intended strong-SDE/process-class identification and moment/localization transfer. L2L^2L2-time continuity alone is insufficient for sample-path continuity; the later explicit Brownian-modification and maximal-limit construction proves simultaneous continuous versions of these actual computed integrals.

Complete proof and source context

Actual selected additive trajectories are adapted

The Picard problem is constructed inside each complete past-measurable L2L^2L2 subspace. The pointwise lifted nonlinear field preserves that subspace. Clamping the original input to the fixed past and using actual common-input uniqueness identifies this constructed trajectory with the selected original solution. No conditional projection is assumed to commute with a nonlinear drift.

The canonical initial sampler and the independent complete particle initial cloud are measurable in their actual constructed initial/noise filtrations. Their physical Brownian inputs are identified exactly with the Driver inputs and proved adapted. The actual selected canonical mean-field sampler and interacting particle realization therefore have current-past measurable L2L^2L2 variables at every time, without an adapted-solution premise. A standard strongly adapted representative is constructed with a.e. equality at each time; a separate theorem now constructs a simultaneous continuous original sampler version when the actual raw additive input has continuous paths.

Complete proof and source context

General state-dependent diffusion realized from martingale increments

Actual continuous L2L^2L2 drift and diffusion columns realize the general model pointwise, retaining parameter- and state-dependent diffusion. The sampler drift residual has a standard martingale representative, the state is adapted, and SynchronousIsometry identifies the weighted residual-increment second moment with the actual diffusion-difference integral. The optimiser follows its original ODE.

These inputs derive the synchronous quadratic weak equation and, under source A3, its energy decay. No energy derivative or pair forward equation is assumed. Observation integrability and norm-continuous L2L^2L2 coefficient realizations are explicit; state second moments alone do not imply the required L2L^2L2 drift integrability for superlinear drifts. Marginal tests are empty and the pair domain the quadratic singleton; the actual computed integrator below now supplies martingale/isometry for arbitrary time-L2L^2L2 adapted columns. The original raw results above derive the appropriate calculus directly; this intermediate weak-generator interface alone does not assert a rich marginal Itô domain.

Complete proof and source context

Source A3 energy and transport decay with integrable coefficients

The actual optimiser follows its original integral equation, the drift is Bochner L1L^1L1 in time with L2L^2L2 random-variable values, and each diffusion column is time-L2L^2L2. The actual sampler residual has a standard martingale representative. Exact quadratic increments derive the full expected energy balance; literal model coefficient identities and the actual joint-law pushforward transfer source A3 into dissipation.

This proves energy decay, actual joint-law RMS contraction and genuine marginal Wasserstein decay for the supplied initial coupling. Continuous coefficients and pointwise optimiser derivatives are unnecessary. The general interface retains actual stochastic weighted increment isometry; that property is independently constructed for arbitrary time-L2L^2L2 adapted finite columns. Extending the intended source A1 solution class to these integral/martingale contracts, including coefficient-moment/localization transfer, remains explicit. Simultaneous continuous versions in the displayed integrable class are now derived below. Source P2\mathcal P_2P2​ state moments alone do not establish all drift coefficient moments.

This works with time-integrable drift, time-L² diffusion and original
integral optimizer equations. Continuous coefficients and pointwise time
derivatives are not required. Stochastic-integral realization and its
synchronous isometry remain explicit inputs; no source A1 equivalence is
asserted by this module.
-/

  (Q : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure Q] (ℱ : Filtration ℝ ‹MeasurableSpace Ω›)

/-- A genuine finite-horizon integral trajectory. All equations concern the
original optimizer and sampler coefficients; no quadratic energy identity
or energy dissipation is a field. -/

variable {Q ℱ} {M : Model S Θ Z X I} {T : ℝ}

/-- Restriction changes no actual trajectory or noise representative. -/

/-- The actual sampler work is the pullback of weighted drift and diffusion
pairings of the realized L² columns. -/


/-- Only Borel measurability of the primitive coefficients is used here. -/




/-- Conditional expectation needs representatives only at its two times.
This supports actual martingales stopped after the finite horizon. -/

/-- Weighted increment orthogonality on two actual finite-horizon times. -/

/-- The full deterministic/L² difference of two actual trajectories. -/






/-- Actual joint law and coefficient realization derive A3 dissipation;
no lifted coefficient inequality is supplied. -/





/-- The full integral decomposition is derived from the original optimizer
equations and the actual sampler drift residuals. -/


/-- Actual synchronous noise energy is the only stochastic-integral
interface. In the completion construction this follows from the proved
weighted increment isometry for the difference of the two integrands. -/

/-- The original optimizer integral equations, actual martingales and
synchronous increment isometry imply the full integral quadratic balance.
No energy balance or differentiability is assumed. -/

/-- Source A3 yields true expected joint quadratic contraction for actual
integral martingale trajectories. Time L¹ drift and time L² diffusion
replace continuous coefficients and pointwise-in-time derivatives. -/

/-- The actual joint optimizer/sampler RMS cost contracts at the paper's
condition-number rate. This is a fixed synchronous realization theorem;
realization of arbitrary prescribed initial couplings is a separate step. -/

/-- The actual joint sampler law has exactly the realized L² coupling cost. -/

/-- Contraction is an actual joint-law RMS statement, rather than a
formal state-space norm that has not been identified with a coupling law. -/

/-- The realized true marginal-law distance is bounded by contraction of
this actual initial coupling. The infimum over arbitrary initial couplings
requires a law-preserving realization construction separately. -/

end PBGSO.IntegralModelContraction

Complete proof and source context

One continuous original additive sampler version for every horizon time

A Bochner L1L^1L1-time family of L2L^2L2 variables now has an actually constructed joint strongly measurable, product-integrable representative. Its literal pathwise primitive, together with the original raw additive input, yields one jointly strongly measurable sampler process with the same L2L^2L2 variable at every horizon time. Product Fubini transfers the original nonlinear drift equation on one spatial full-measure event for all times, and the paths are continuous there.

The direct mean-field theorem derives all drift realization and regularity from the actual global integral solution and primitive LipschitzDynamics. The remaining additional input is explicit: the raw additive input is jointly strongly measurable, represents the actual L2L^2L2 input at every horizon time, and has almost-sure continuous paths. The later actual Brownian-modification construction derives this condition from primitive Driver laws, and the final computed-model corollary discharges it internally. Combining the exact version identity with proved L2L^2L2 adaptation gives AE current-past measurability of the same version; strict adaptation under an uncompleted natural filtration is not asserted.

Complete proof and source context

Constructed continuous Brownian drivers and original sampler paths

Actual Gaussian fourth moments yield summable adjacent dyadic-grid tails. Borel–Cantelli and literal polygon interpolation derive continuous limits. An explicit strict-past series is adapted to the original filtration; countable-horizon overlap then constructs a globally continuous Brownian modification with the same random variable at every fixed time. Spatial increment independence and full future–past independence are preserved by proved almost-everywhere identities.

The original and modified Drivers have the exact same filtration, and the computed stochastic integral is proved invariant under this modification. Consequently every actual closed integral has a simultaneous continuous martingale version, and original model Data has one joint continuous sampler/noise realization satisfying its original nonlinear drift equation at every horizon time on a single probability-one event.

No Brownian continuity premise remains in these final statements. The original model drift must be jointly strongly measurable on the chosen horizon; actual pathwise drift integrability is derived from its time-L1L^1L1(L2L^2L2) contract. The selected joint sampler is proved AE adapted at every time; the constructed Brownian modification itself is strictly adapted to the original uncompleted filtration. Original raw Brownian representatives are not asserted to have continuous paths. Minimal source A1 localization remains separate.

Actual constant diffusion matching and independent-copy seeds

Every finite family of constant diffusion columns determines a genuine continuous linear map from Euclidean noise. Its constructed normalized map exactly cancels the square-root-two scaling of the Brownian input constructor. The model column identity is proved for every constant-diffusion compatible model; no matrix-matching equality is assumed.

Separately, finite product sampling of complete one-copy seeds proves the actual fixed-time iid reference-cloud law and independence of whole coordinate trajectories. Those seeds may include the initial variable and its noise. Their L2L^2L2 coordinate pullbacks are genuine isometries. Identifying these variables with the intended reference equations and shared-driver particle/copy system remains a process obligation; no independence of interacting particles is inferred.

Energy decay and finite-particle comparison mechanism

For a supplied continuous nonnegative energy with a right derivative, Lean proves the comparison from E′≤−2ρEE'\le-2\rho EE′≤−2ρE, and the regularized square-root comparison from E(0)=0E(0)=0E(0)=0 and

E′(t)≤−2ρE(t)+2cE(t)⟹E(t)≤cρ(1−e−ρt).E'(t)\le-2\rho E(t)+2c\sqrt{E(t)}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \sqrt{E(t)}\le\frac c\rho(1-e^{-\rho t}).E′(t)≤−2ρE(t)+2cE(t)​⟹E(t)​≤ρc​(1−e−ρt).

The proof differentiates E+ε2\sqrt{E+\varepsilon^2}E+ε2​ and removes ε\varepsilonε, so it does not assume differentiability of E\sqrt EE​ at zero. Metric comparisons yield the κ\sqrt\kappaκ​ factor. A separate theorem derives the energy inequality from actual common-additive-input integral equations and transformed drift monotonicity. Another module proves the i.i.d. variance identity on the finite product law. WeakContraction separately derives the full state-dependent synchronous-generator energy identity from its actual quadratic test equation. LawContraction takes the infimum over genuine initial couplings and proves the exact optimiser–law distance contraction and stationary uniqueness. The actual constructed integral modules below derive synchronous law realizations in their explicit integrability class. These scalar and weak-generator statements are intermediate interfaces. The original raw-process theorems above derive their required calculus and physical reference assembly under the named source assumptions.

/-!
# Quantitative comparison arguments for PBGSO

The model and joint monotonicity definition retain general optimiser maps,
augmented sampler states, and multiplicative noise. The comparison theorems
below prove the deterministic analytic step of the paper's arguments from
explicit energy derivative hypotheses. Identifying such derivatives with
coupled stochastic laws requires a separate Itô/martingale argument; that
argument is not silently included in these hypotheses or claimed here.
-/

open MeasureTheory Set Filter
open scoped BigOperators RealInnerProductSpace InnerProductSpace Topology

namespace PBGSO

section Geometry
variable {S Θ Z X I : Type*}
  [NormedAddCommGroup S] [InnerProductSpace ℝ S]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Θ] [NormedSpace ℝ Θ]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Z] [InnerProductSpace ℝ Z]
  [MeasurableSpace Z] [Fintype I]

/-- Explicit positive-definite quadratic weights and their spectral bounds.
No symmetry or definiteness is inferred from an arbitrary matrix. -/

namespace TwistedGeometry
variable (D : TwistedGeometry S Z)





end TwistedGeometry

/-- The two marginals are specified by genuine pushforwards. -/

/-- The sampler contribution to the twisted quadratic coupling energy.
The sum is the weighted Hilbert--Schmidt diffusion correction. -/

/-- The exact twisted joint strong monotonicity assumption in the paper,
including the Hilbert--Schmidt diffusion correction represented by its
finite sum of squared column norms. The gradient integrability premises
exclude accidental use of undefined Bochner expectations. -/

end Geometry

/-- Grönwall proves the squared-energy decay from a right derivative
inequality. This theorem applies to any energy, including an expectation
once differentiation under the stochastic integral has been justified. -/

/-- The square-root comparison needed for the finite-particle theorem.
It is proved from the *squared* energy inequality and zero initial error.
No differentiability of `sqrt E` at its zeros is assumed: the proof uses
`sqrt (E + ε²)` and then sends `ε` to zero by an order argument. -/

/-- The condition-number factor follows from the two quadratic norm
comparisons; the estimate is on the root mean square distance. -/

/-- The diagonal-dominance sufficient condition in Appendix A. It controls
the optimiser--sampler cross term as part of one joint quadratic form. -/

/-- A sharp completion-of-squares criterion for the 2×2 small-gain matrix.
It can be used with any certified lower eigenvalue `ρ`. -/

/-- Combining particle interaction and mean-field relaxation gives the
paper's parameter bound; the triangle premise is explicitly separate. -/

/-- The exponential relaxation factor tends to zero at every positive
contractivity rate. -/

/-- A finite distance between two stationary solutions is zero if the
same contraction estimate holds for every nonnegative elapsed time. -/

/-- The explicit right-hand side of the paper's parameter estimate has the
stated long-time sampling floor. No discretisation term is included. -/

/-- The sampling floor vanishes as the number of particles tends to
infinity, with all geometry and variance constants fixed. -/

end PBGSO

Actual empirical couplings and particle work

Pairing particle iii with reference particle iii produces a genuine empirical coupling. Its quadratic cost is the average of the paired squared distances, so

W22(νN,νˉ[N])≤N−1∑i∥Zi−Zˉi∥2.W_2^2(\nu^N,\bar\nu^{[N]})\le N^{-1}\sum_i\|Z_i-\bar Z_i\|^2.W22​(νN,νˉ[N])≤N−1i∑​∥Zi​−Zˉi​∥2.

Positive NNN is explicit; no independence of the interacting cloud is assumed. The law-level joint condition is lifted to the actual finite averaged force and synchronous diffusion correction. The population-gradient discrepancy is exactly the empirical reference observation fluctuation. These facts do not identify the dynamically evolved reference cloud with an independent product law; that process-law obligation remains separate.

/-! # Lifting the general law-level condition to actual empirical clouds

The pairing measure here is the actual empirical law of the paired particle
coordinates. Its two marginals are proved equal to the empirical cloud laws.
Joint monotonicity therefore applies to the actual finite-particle force and
the averaged synchronous diffusion correction, without an independence premise
for the interacting particles.
-/

open scoped BigOperators RealInnerProductSpace
namespace PBGSO

section Empirical
variable {E F B : Type*} [MeasurableSpace E] [MeasurableSingletonClass E]
  [MeasurableSpace F] [NormedAddCommGroup B] [NormedSpace ℝ B]

/-- All functions into a normed space are integrable against a nonempty
finite empirical law. No regularity or global growth condition is needed. -/

/-- Empirical integration is exactly the arithmetic mean. -/

/-- Pushforward commutes with the actual finite empirical law. -/

end Empirical

variable {S Θ Z X I : Type*}
  [NormedAddCommGroup S] [InnerProductSpace ℝ S]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Θ] [NormedSpace ℝ Θ] [CompleteSpace Θ]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Z] [InnerProductSpace ℝ Z]
  [MeasurableSpace Z] [MeasurableSingletonClass Z] [Fintype I]

/-- Pairing particle i with reference particle i is an actual measure
coupling. This property does not require the arrays to be independent. -/

/-- The actual averaged twisted separation of two finite clouds. -/

/-- The empirical joint work, including the full weighted diffusion
correction for each synchronously driven sampler. -/

/-- The law-level joint condition lifts to the actual finite empirical
cloud with exactly the same rate and normalisation. -/

/-- The only additional term when the reference optimiser uses the
population gradient is its actual empirical observation fluctuation. -/

end PBGSO

/-!
# From actual coupling energies to Wasserstein laws

The transport distance is the infimum over all genuine initial couplings.
No optimal-coupling existence or supplied Wasserstein conclusion is assumed.
The generic energy theorem takes actual output couplings and their quadratic
energy comparisons; coupled-generator or integral-equation arguments can
produce those data. Realising the same output laws from every initial coupling
is an explicit process-level requirement of that theorem.

The additive specialisation below applies to actual integral solutions of
the independent general observation/response/sampler maps. It derives the
sampler law bound from their proved common-input contraction. State-dependent
strong-SDE and martingale-problem equivalence are separate requirements.
-/

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set
open scoped NNReal ENNReal Topology
namespace PBGSO

section CouplingCost
variable {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H]
  [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H]

omit [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] in
/-- The genuine coupling cost squared is its quadratic integral, whenever
the difference has a finite second moment. -/

omit [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] in
/-- Finite-second-moment marginals make every coupling cost finite; this
does not require the coupling to be independent or optimal. -/

omit [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] in
/-- A finite actual joint law bounds the ordinary real-valued transport
distance without converting infinity to zero. -/

omit [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H]
  [SecondCountableTopology H] in
/-- The first norm moment is at most the root second moment on a probability
space. Applied to the actual coupling difference, this supplies the
characteristic-function estimate used for separation of transport laws. -/

/-- The characteristic functions of the two marginal laws are controlled by
the cost of any finite coupling. -/

/-- Pairing particle i with particle i gives the finite empirical
Wasserstein bound. The proof uses the genuine empirical pair measure and
computes its quadratic transport cost exactly; no particle independence is
assumed. The positive particle count makes the two empirical measures laws. -/

variable [CompleteSpace H]

/-- Zero quadratic transport separates probability laws. The proof chooses
arbitrarily small finite couplings from the defining infimum and compares
characteristic functions; no optimal coupling is assumed. -/

/-- The real transport distance can be used for equality only after its
finiteness has been established explicitly. -/

end CouplingCost

section InfimumBridge
variable {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H]
  [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H]

/-- Actual quadratic coupling energies give the condition-number prefactor
after taking the infimum over all initial couplings. The family contains
output joint laws, not a supplied Wasserstein bound or an optimal coupling. -/

omit [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] in
/-- Finite couplings whose costs converge to the defining transport
infimum. Attainment of that infimum is unnecessary. -/

omit [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] in
/-- Any continuous bound in the actual initial coupling cost passes to the
optimal transport infimum. This also supports the mixed deterministic-law
quadratic metric, whose square root is not affine. -/

end InfimumBridge

section WeakLaws
variable {S Θ Z X I : Type*}
  [NormedAddCommGroup S] [InnerProductSpace ℝ S]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Θ] [NormedSpace ℝ Θ]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Z] [InnerProductSpace ℝ Z]
  [MeasurableSpace Z] [BorelSpace Z] [SecondCountableTopology Z] [Fintype I]

/-- The paper's Euclidean product distance between a deterministic full
optimiser state and a sampler law. Its transport component is a genuine
infimum over all couplings. Finiteness is proved in its use below. -/

/-- The full multiplicative-noise weak-generator contraction passes to the
optimal law distance. The process hypothesis is an actual synchronous weak
solution with the specified marginal trajectories for every initial coupling;
it is not an energy inequality or a Wasserstein-bound hypothesis. The
quadratic separation test must explicitly belong to the generator domain. -/

/-- Stationary uniqueness is a law equality, obtained by decay and the
separation property of the transport infimum. Existence of the stationary
weak laws and of their synchronous realizations remains explicit. -/

end WeakLaws

namespace LipschitzDynamics

  [NormedAddCommGroup Z] [NormedSpace ℝ Z] [CompleteSpace Z]
  [MeasurableSpace Z] [BorelSpace Z] [SecondCountableTopology Z]
  [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace ℝ G] [CompleteSpace G]
  [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H]

  (D : PBGSO.LipschitzDynamics A Z G)

/-- Constructed actual general additive integral solutions contract their
deterministic optimiser and sampler laws. The initial sampler cost here is
the selected L² coupling. Optimising that cost across law-preserving
realisations is performed separately by `bound_of_all_finite_couplings`.
The norm on the Banach product is the maximum norm, made explicit by `max`. -/

end LipschitzDynamics
end PBGSO

import PBGSO.WeakContraction
import PBGSO.EmpiricalMonotonicity

/-! # The actual particle/copy synchronous generator

Full finite-particle interaction bound from the actual generator

The actual paired interacting/reference generator retains the complete state-dependent diffusion. Its quadratic forward equation, joint monotonicity, weighted Cauchy–Schwarz and the exact i.i.d.-cloud variance give

Exact additional premises. Positive NNN and ρ\rhoρ; a particle/copy weak forward equation whose test domain contains the actual quadratic energy; zero initial coupling energy; an almost-surely deterministic reference optimiser; an actual reference-cloud marginal equal to the finite product of its common law; square-integrable observations; uniform centred variance VVV; optimiser response Lipschitz constant LΨL_\PsiLΨ​; and the stated residual and empirical-metric AE measurability. EmpiricalMeasurability derives the actual Wasserstein statistic’s measurability for all joint laws in Borel second-countable Hilbert coordinates, discharging that metric contract. The forced-energy derivative and dissipation are derived, not assumed. Separate helper theorems derive residual AE measurability from the primitive response bound and actual iid reference marginal, and zero initial energy from synchronous initial coordinates. The interacting cloud need not be independent of itself or of the reference cloud. Translating source strong solutions and their dynamic independent copies into these generator and marginal contracts remains separate. The bound concerns interaction against the independent-copy empirical law; a population-law Wasserstein bound needs an additional empirical sampling term.

Constructed additive interacting/copy particle data

Starting with an actual global one-copy integral reference, finite product seeds construct independent complete reference trajectories. The shared-optimiser interacting process is then constructed globally from the true finite empirical force and the same additive inputs. Its particle/copy quadratic generator equation, exact iid reference-cloud marginal, deterministic reference optimiser, observation square integrability, residual measurability and zero initial error are derived.

The final ParticleParameterApproximation is a constructed output. Positive particle count, primitive global Lipschitz maps, autonomous response and constant diffusion compatibility, continuous input starting at zero and the uniform observation-variance bound remain inputs. The generator domain is the particle quadratic singleton; this is an actual additive process theorem, without claiming a full marginal Itô equation or state-dependent strong-SDE realization.

Actual random-parameter bound and joint large-time/large-particle limit

The frozen target constant weak solution is constructed from its stationary generator, zero mean observation and optimiser fixed point. Full mean-field law contraction and the particle generator forcing are then combined with an internally proved L2L^2L2 triangle inequality and a one-Lipschitz parameter projection:

∥PθstN−Pθs⋆∥L2≤κe−ρtd0+LΨρκVN(1−e−ρt).\|P_\theta s_t^N-P_\theta s_\star\|_{L^2}\le\sqrt\kappa e^{-\rho t}d_0+\frac{L_\Psi}{\rho}\sqrt{\frac{\kappa V}{N}}(1-e^{-\rho t}).∥Pθ​stN​−Pθ​s⋆​∥L2​≤κ​e−ρtd0​+ρLΨ​​NκV​​(1−e−ρt).

The proof establishes square integrability of the actual parameter error. It retains the explicit mean-field and particle/copy weak equations, quadratic generator domains, frozen stationary-target integrability, zero mean observation, optimiser fixed point at every nonnegative time, all-initial-coupling synchronous realization, actual iid reference cloud, uniform variance and the response/measurability/initial-energy contracts. No parameter-error, triangle or final rate premise is supplied. A uniform family satisfying these contracts has actual error tending to zero jointly as time and particle count tend to infinity; its positive count is indexed by n+1n+1n+1. This is a conditional weak-process theorem, with the strong-SDE realization bridge still explicit. The target is the source critical point; minimization needs its own assumption.

Separate primitive conditions in the actual coupling integral

The primitive assumptions are same-law optimiser dissipation with rate rOr_OrO​, optimiser response Lipschitz constant LΨL_\PsiLΨ​, sampler observation Lipschitz constant LFL_FLF​, frozen-sampler dissipation rSr_SrS​, parameter drift Lipschitz constant LbL_bLb​ and a full squared diffusion-column bound with constant LσL_\sigmaLσ​. This proves full law-level twisted joint monotonicity. Require the displayed rate to be positive for exponential contraction; this is exactly the source simpler diagonal condition. The full determinant criterion is proved below, including its equality with the actual minimum eigenvalue of the literal source matrix. No combined optimiser/sampler work estimate is assumed in place of the primitive conditions.

/-! # The projected source criterion with its explicit finite signed domain
The source U5 sampler inequality contains a signed drift-work integral for
every P2 coupling. Reading those integrals as finite is stated independently
of the inequality. Constant diffusion turns this domain directly into the
universal finite-work convention needed by the constant-noise law theorem.
-/

  [Fintype x] [DecidableEq x] [Nonempty x] [Fintype v] [DecidableEq v] [Fintype I]

/-- Explicit ordinary finite signed-integral domain of the universal U5
sampler inequality. This is not a consequence of the conditional inequality. -/

/-- No stochastic energy conclusion is assumed: constant columns cancel
algebraically, so the U5 finite domain gives precisely finite sampler work. -/

signed integrals. The domain is visible, not inferred from monotonicity. -/

import PBGSO.ProjectedCriteria
import Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.Order
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.ContinuousFunctionalCalculus.Rpow.Basic

/-!
# Generalized spectral lower bounds for positive definite matrices

The minimum is taken over the actual finite spectrum of the whitened
matrix `D^(-1/2) K D^(-1/2)`. Positive definiteness and the quadratic
comparison are derived from the primitive SPD hypotheses.
-/

noncomputable section
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
open Matrix
open scoped MatrixOrder Matrix.Norms.L2Operator BigOperators
namespace PBGSO.GeneralizedSpectrum

variable {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n]

/-- The smallest actual eigenvalue of a finite real symmetric matrix.
Nonempty coordinates are explicit because the empty spectrum has no minimum. -/



/-- The minimum is attained by an actual eigenvalue. -/

/-- This definition is precisely the least point of the real matrix
spectrum, not merely an arbitrary certified eigenvalue lower bound. -/

/-- Spectral diagonalization proves that subtracting the minimum eigenvalue
times the identity leaves a positive semidefinite matrix. -/

/-- The spectral lower bound is an actual quadratic-form inequality. -/

/-- The matrix appearing in the source generalized-eigenvalue rate. -/


/-- Whitening preserves strict positive definiteness because the actual
positive square root is invertible. -/

/-- The exact source rate, the minimum generalized eigenvalue. -/


/-- Congruence by the actual positive square root converts the spectral
lower bound back to `K - rho D ≥ 0`. -/

/-- The exact generalized minimum eigenvalue controls the primitive
quadratic forms, for every coordinate vector. -/

/-- The chosen inverse square root is exactly the square root of the
inverse matrix, matching the source's `D^{-1/2}` notation. -/

end PBGSO.GeneralizedSpectrum

open GeneralizedSpectrum MeasureTheory
open scoped InnerProductSpace RealInnerProductSpace

section Projected

  [NormedAddCommGroup S] [InnerProductSpace ℝ S]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Θ] [InnerProductSpace ℝ Θ] [CompleteSpace Θ]
  [NormedAddCommGroup Z] [InnerProductSpace ℝ Z] [MeasurableSpace Z] [BorelSpace Z]
  [NormedAddCommGroup X] [InnerProductSpace ℝ X]
  [NormedAddCommGroup U] [InnerProductSpace ℝ U]
  [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [Fintype I]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n] [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] [Nonempty m]

/-- The projected criterion at the exact source generalized-eigenvalue
rate. Matrix equalities identify the two metrics and the projected-plus-
auxiliary quadratic forms in explicit coordinates; they do not assume the
final lower comparison. The SPD inputs prove that comparison spectrally. -/

end Projected

η=1+2L2/(rγ2)2,ε=1−η,A=L2ηγ2,c=r−2A,ρ=min⁡(c,ε)γ+1+2/γ>0.\eta=\frac{1+2L^2/(r\gamma^2)}2,\quad \varepsilon=1-\eta,\quad A=\frac{L^2}{\eta\gamma^2},\quad c=r-2A,\quad \rho=\frac{\min(c,\varepsilon)}{\gamma+1+2/\gamma}>0.η=21+2L2/(rγ2)​,ε=1−η,A=ηγ2L2​,c=r−2A,ρ=γ+1+2/γmin(c,ε)​>0.

The metric lower constant is min⁡{γ/4,1/(2γ)}\min\{\gamma/4,1/(2\gamma)\}min{γ/4,1/(2γ)} and its upper constant is γ+1+2/γ\gamma+1+2/\gammaγ+1+2/γ. Separate auxiliary dissipation and all coupling score/position/auxiliary integrability estimates are proved from the primitive hypotheses.
