import PBGSO.ProjectedCriteria
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.ProdL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Lp.MeasurableSpace

/-!
# Explicit feasible hypocoercive coefficients

The strict source friction threshold is converted into concrete Young,
auxiliary, metric and decay constants. No coefficient feasibility or
positive-definiteness assertion is assumed. The forces need not be gradients.
-/

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory
open scoped InnerProductSpace RealInnerProductSpace NNReal
namespace PBGSO


/-- The manuscript's displayed square-root friction condition implies
the polynomial threshold used by the coefficient proofs. -/

/-- The squared version of the exact source threshold produces an explicit
Young parameter strictly between zero and one. -/

/-- Both auxiliary dissipation and the projected coefficient have strictly
positive room under the source threshold. -/




section Hilbert
variable {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H]

/-- A concrete lower norm constant for the source's actual twisted metric. -/

/-- Young's inequality gives exactly the separate U5 auxiliary estimate
with the explicitly chosen coefficients. -/

/-- A globally monotone and Lipschitz joint force has a completely explicit
positive hypocoercive contraction rate under the source friction threshold.
This is a deterministic drift estimate for the actual metric pairing. -/

end Hilbert

/-- Euclidean product of position and momentum coordinates. -/

section Metric
variable {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H]

/-- The actual source block matrix `[[gamma I,I],[I,2/gamma I]]`
as a bounded linear operator on the Hilbert phase space. -/




/-- Multiplication of the actual block operator by the actual heavy-ball
vector field gives the previously proved scalar pairing identity. -/

end Metric

/-- Both optimiser and sampler metrics are constructed explicitly, with
certified symmetry and quantitative positive definiteness. -/

section Jensen
variable {Ω H : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H]
  [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H]

/-- The square-norm Jensen inequality follows from integrating a
nonnegative squared distance. This supplies the optimiser-force estimate
from its actual Bochner expectation. -/

end Jensen

section HeavyBall
variable {A X I : Type*}
  [NormedAddCommGroup A] [InnerProductSpace ℝ A] [CompleteSpace A]
  [NormedAddCommGroup X] [InnerProductSpace ℝ X]
  [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [SecondCountableTopology X] [Fintype I]

/-- The actual unit-mass heavy-ball optimiser and underdamped sampler.
The observation and negative score are independent maps. Constant diffusion
is arbitrary, allowing the exact source column matrix as a special case. -/

/-- The source position and momentum projections, with the explicitly
chosen positive auxiliary weights. -/

/-- The optimiser vector-field difference really is the heavy-ball block
applied to the state and actual mean-gradient differences. -/

/-- The sampler difference is the corresponding negative-score heavy-ball
block, without any conservative-potential assumption. -/

/-- The joint Lipschitz bound gives the Jensen estimate for the *actual*
mean-gradient difference through every coupling of the sampler laws. -/


/-- The full source hypocoercive criterion for the actual heavy-ball
optimiser and underdamped sampler. The two component Lipschitz bounds are
primitive projected-field bounds; all U5 constants, metric definiteness and
the positive decay rate are derived. The remaining explicit analytic input
is integrability of the coupling score/auxiliary expressions. -/

/-- In the globally Lipschitz heavy-ball example the integrability needed
by the general projected criterion is itself a theorem. The supplied
coupling energy controls both position and momentum squares; Young's
inequality then controls the score work. -/

/-- End-to-end verification of the source hypocoercive *criterion*, from
pointwise projected monotonicity, joint force bounds and the displayed
friction threshold. No U5, metric, rate-feasibility, Jensen, coupling-gradient
or score-integrability conclusion is assumed in this theorem. This remains
an algebraic/law criterion, separate from an SDE existence or Itô theorem. -/

/-- The source projected field, as an actual map of the Hilbert product. -/

/-- A Lipschitz bound for the complete projected field yields the component
square bounds used in the preceding theorem. -/

/-- The appendix hypocoercive proposition with its original joint
Lipschitz hypothesis and square-root friction threshold, with an explicit
metric and positive rate. Constant sampler diffusion is arbitrary. -/

end HeavyBall
end PBGSO

Complete proof and source context

Both implementation drifts construct actual general models

The M-MFPO model has complete Hilbert optimiser (θ,m)(\theta,m)(θ,m) and sampler (x,v)(x,v)(x,v); the HOL model has optimiser θ\thetaθ and nested Hilbert sampler (x,u,v)(x,u,v)(x,u,v), with drift (u,−G+γv,−γu−αv)(u,-G+\gamma v,-\gamma u-\alpha v)(u,−G+γv,−γu−αv) and noise only in the last sampler coordinate. The original FFF and GGG remain independent maps.

Separate primitive global Lipschitz bounds construct the full mean-field LipschitzDynamics, actual model compatibility and one-Lipschitz parameter projection. Both raw finite-empirical integral drifts intertwine exactly with those model drifts. No unrelated model equations or common potential are assumed. Source joint monotonicity, frozen invariance, variance and intended Brownian implementation remain their own hypotheses.

are constructed. Auxiliary variables use genuine Hilbert product norms; no

end Helpers

  (hG : ∀ a b x y, ‖G a x - G b y‖ ≤ (LG : ℝ) * (‖a - b‖ + ‖x - y‖))
  (γ : ℝ)

/-- Actual M-MFPO primitive maps, with all Lipschitz constants derived from
F/G and friction. The optimiser state is (parameter,momentum). -/

/-- The source optimiser parameter projection is actually nonexpansive. -/
end Momentum

end HigherOrder

Complete proof and source context

Continuous and discrete frictionless volume preservation

The discrete force kicks and position drifts preserve product Haar measure for arbitrary measurable forces. For a globally differentiable force in finite dimension, their actual shear derivatives and the chain rule also prove signed determinant one for the original B ⁣− ⁣A ⁣− ⁣BB\!-\!A\!-\!BB−A−B implementation. For an arbitrary C1C^1C1 position force and actual globally defined frictionless ODE trajectories, the continuous proof derives joint C1C^1C1 flow dependence, its variational equation and determinant derivative, then proves

det⁡DΦt(x)=1.\det D\Phi_t(x)=1.detDΦt​(x)=1.

The source flow assumptions suffice. Supply only the C1C^1C1 force, actual ODE at every time and state, and identity initial map. Joint continuity and differentiability of the flow, a variational equation, globally Lipschitz cutoff fields and determinant preservation are derived. The proof constructs genuine globally Lipschitz cutoff trajectories, proves local equality near each compact orbit and transfers the path-space Picard/implicit-function regularity. ODE uniqueness also derives the group identity and negative-time inverse. Jacobian change of variables then proves literal Lebesgue MeasurePreserving for every real-time slice, with no injectivity or inverse premise. The joint force may be nonconservative. Friction and stochastic thermostat steps are outside these claims.

/-- C¹ regularity of actual parameterized fixed points follows from the

M-MFPO: new verified map bounds

For the concrete OBABO map, let eee be the sum of position and momentum discrepancies, assume the coupled force is globally LLL-Lipschitz with L≥0L\ge0L≥0, and let the thermostat satisfy ∣η∣≤1|\eta|\le1∣η∣≤1. With

A=(1+∣h∣L/2)2(1+∣h∣),A=(1+|h|L/2)^2(1+|h|),A=(1+∣h∣L/2)2(1+∣h∣),

the proved map estimate is

en+1≤Aen+∣σ∣(A∥Δξn∥+∥Δξn′∥).e_{n+1}\le A e_n+|\sigma|\big(A\|\Delta\xi_n\|+\|\Delta\xi'_n\|\big).en+1​≤Aen​+∣σ∣(A∥Δξn​∥+∥Δξn′​∥).

If each innovation discrepancy is at most ε\varepsilonε, the verified finite-step bound is en≤Ane0+∣σ∣(A+1)ε∑j=0n−1Aje_n\le A^ne_0+|\sigma|(A+1)\varepsilon\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}A^jen​≤Ane0​+∣σ∣(A+1)ε∑j=0n−1​Aj. The recurrence is derived by composing the exact kick, drift and thermostat maps. These new bounds give robustness and finite-horizon stability; AAA can exceed one. They do not establish convergence to the optimum or invariant Gibbs law. The optimiser's noise coordinate is zero.

/-!
# New pathwise bounds for the two PBGSO implementation methods

The bounds in this file concern the **actual discrete update maps**. They do not
assert a Gibbs target, a stochastic stationary law, or an optimal mixing rate.
Forces in the optimiser and sampler may be unrelated. Supplied innovations are
arbitrary vectors: consequently the estimates also hold samplewise for Gaussian
innovations, without assuming that the optimiser receives thermal noise.
-/

namespace PBGSO
namespace Methods

variable {E Θ X : Type*}
variable [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
variable [NormedAddCommGroup Θ] [NormedSpace ℝ Θ]
variable [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X]

/-- The sum norm on a momentum-position difference, independent of the ambient
product space's max norm. The order is `(momentum, position)`. -/

/-- Triangle inequality for the explicit sum of coordinate errors. -/

/-- A finite geometric sum, which remains defined at amplification factor one. -/

/-- Iteration with a possibly time-dependent innovation. -/

/-- Finite accumulation used below. Each application proves its recurrence
from concrete maps, rather than assuming it as a modelling hypothesis. -/




/-- The force kick has an explicit Lipschitz amplification factor. -/

/-- The drift shear has amplification at most `1+|h|`. -/

/-- A damped thermostat is nonexpansive with synchronous innovations, and its
response to innovation perturbation is exactly controlled by `|σ|`. -/

/-- The general coupled force. `Fbar` is the empirical optimiser force and `G`
is the sampler force, usually `∇ₓE`; no common potential is imposed. -/

/-- The paper's M-MFPO OBABO map. A particle innovation has zero optimiser
coordinate; hence both optimiser thermostat stages are deterministic. -/

/-- An explicit conservative amplification coefficient for a BAB stage. -/

/-- New one-step OBABO robustness estimate. Its force Lipschitz hypothesis is
on the arbitrary coupled vector field, not a joint-potential Hessian. -/

/-- New finite-step perturbation bound for the concrete OBABO map. For a
synchronous coupling (`ε=0`) the initial discrepancy is multiplied by `A^n`.
The estimate is finite horizon stability, not a claim that `A<1`. -/

/-- Finite-horizon accumulation only requires the local estimate on steps
strictly preceding the requested endpoint. -/

end Methods
end PBGSO

A further new theorem compares the actual OBABO trajectory against compatible kinetic integral-solution segments. These reference, moment, modulus and noise conditions are required only on the used segments k<nk<nk<n.

en≤Ane0+(R+B+23(L+γ+1)Rhh)∑j=0n−1Aj.e_n\le A^n e_0+\left(\mathcal R+B+\tfrac23(L+\gamma+1)Rh\sqrt h\right)\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}A^j.en​≤Ane0​+(R+B+32​(L+γ+1)Rhh​)j=0∑n−1​Aj.

The local defect is proved by expanding the concrete map and integrating the reference modulus. All coefficient, force, momentum and innovation terms are explicit in the adjacent definitions and signature. The norms may themselves be L2L^2L2 norms, but Brownian existence, covariance coupling and the required moment/modulus estimates must be established for that stochastic application. M-MFPO: explicit square-root-step rate

For the physical coefficients η=e−γh/2\eta=e^{-\gamma h/2}η=e−γh/2, σ=1−e−γh\sigma=\sqrt{1-e^{-\gamma h}}σ=1−e−γh​, take L,γ≥0L,\gamma\ge0L,γ≥0, 0<h≤10<h\le10<h≤1, a globally LLL-Lipschitz force, compatible kinetic integral-reference segments, grid momentum and force bounds P,F≥0P,F\ge0P,F≥0, a reference increment modulus RtR\sqrt tRt​, and bounds ∥ξ∥,∥ξ′∥≤Ξ\|\xi\|,\|\xi'\|\le\Xi∥ξ∥,∥ξ′∥≤Ξ. The reference full increment is explicitly matched to γh(ξ+ξ′)\sqrt{\gamma h}(\xi+\xi')γh​(ξ+ξ′). Set

KM=1+2L+L2/2,DM=γ2+γ2P+γ+12F+L2(P+Ξ+F/2).K_M=1+2L+L^2/2,\qquad D_M=\tfrac{\gamma^2+\gamma}{2}P+\tfrac{\gamma+1}{2}F+\tfrac L2(P+\Xi+F/2).KM​=1+2L+L2/2,DM​=2γ2+γ​P+2γ+1​F+2L​(P+Ξ+F/2).

The verified finite-horizon estimate is

en≤eKMnh[e0+(DM+γ Ξ+32γγ Ξ+23(L+γ+1)R)(nh)h].e_n\le e^{K_Mnh}\left[e_0+\left(D_M+\sqrt\gamma\,\Xi+ \tfrac32\gamma\sqrt\gamma\,\Xi+\tfrac23(L+\gamma+1)R\right)(nh)\sqrt h\right].en​≤eKM​nh[e0​+(DM​+γ​Ξ+23​γγ​Ξ+32​(L+γ+1)R)(nh)h​].

The proof derives the damping and noise coefficient remainders, and bounds the net two-stage innovation mismatch by 32γγ Ξhh\tfrac32\gamma\sqrt\gamma\,\Xi h\sqrt h23​γγ​Ξhh​. It does not assume a numerical error recurrence. The headline raw-particle L2L^2L2 theorem uses L=2max⁡(LF,LG)L=2\max(L_F,L_G)L=2max(LF​,LG​), where LF=D.meanLipL_F=\mathtt{D.meanLip}LF​=D.meanLip and LG=D.samplerForceLipL_G=\mathtt{D.samplerForceLip}LG​=D.samplerForceLip are derived from the primitive force bounds and cloud encoding, and Ξ=d\Xi=\sqrt dΞ=d​ for the full encoded cloud dimension. It uses actual normalized half increments. Their sum is identified with the scaled full Brownian increment, and their iid Gaussian sequence law requires independent coordinate grid paths. The reference integral equation and its force/momentum and modulus bounds remain explicit, only for k<nk<nk<n. Uniform bounds over meshes give the square-root-step rate on a fixed horizon.

Actual raw-particle implementation. ParticleMethodLp constructs the empirical and sampler force lifts, proves their pointwise identities almost everywhere, and identifies the full OBABO map with the raw nonlinear particle step. The headline theorem applies the Gaussian bound to those proved lifts, including a shared random optimiser and zero optimiser innovations. A continuous linear cloud encoding with inverse is explicit; the supplied Euclidean encoding repacks the particle and spatial indices. The paper's independent isotropic particle innovations use the flattened index Fin⁡(N)×J\operatorname{Fin}(N)\times JFin(N)×J and that explicit Euclidean encoding. An arbitrary invertible encoding transforms the raw noise and does not automatically preserve isotropy. Reference integral equations and finite-horizon moments/moduli remain assumptions. No stationary-target or infinite-horizon claim is made.

import PBGSO.GaussianMethodBounds

/-!
# Pointwise L² lifting of the original finite-particle implementation forces

The optimiser is a random coordinate on the same probability space as every
particle. The cloud encoding is an explicit continuous linear equivalence;
it permits a Euclidean Gaussian cloud to represent the paper's particle array.
The empirical force and sampler force are constructed from the original `F`
and `G`. Their pointwise identification is proved, not postulated.
-/

  [NormedAddCommGroup A] [NormedSpace ℝ A]
  [NormedAddCommGroup C] [NormedSpace ℝ C]
  (Q : Measure Ω)

/-- Pair two random variables on their shared probability space, retaining
all dependence between the optimiser and the particle cloud. -/

/-- The L² pairing is the actual pointwise pair almost everywhere. -/



/-- The joint L² difference is controlled by the sum of marginal L² norms;
no independence between those marginals is used. -/

/-- Evaluate a pair of L² coordinates on their shared sample. -/

/-- Evaluate both momentum and position coordinates. -/




/-- OU stage correspondence is ordinary L² arithmetic; in particular a zero
optimiser innovation stays zero almost everywhere. -/

/-- The position drift stage has exactly the intended pointwise action. -/

/-- Evaluate all four higher-order coordinates on one shared sample. -/

/-- Finite L² affine arithmetic has its usual pointwise interpretation. -/

end Pair

/-- Primitive raw finite-particle data, including an explicit cloud encoding.
The two forces need not derive from a joint potential. -/

namespace ParticleForceData
variable {Ω A X C : Type*} {N : ℕ} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  [NormedAddCommGroup A] [NormedSpace ℝ A]
  [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X]
  [NormedAddCommGroup C] [NormedSpace ℝ C]
  (D : ParticleForceData A X C N)

/-- The actual empirical optimiser force in the supplied cloud coordinates. -/

/-- The actual per-particle sampler force, repacked in cloud coordinates. -/

/-- Explicit raw and lifted force constants, including the cloud coordinate
change. A product L² pairing will use these same constants. -/

/-- The empirical raw map is globally Lipschitz from the primitive force
assumption. No regularity of a numerical error sequence is assumed. -/

/-- The raw sampler map is globally Lipschitz with an explicit encoding cost. -/

section Random
variable (Q : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]

/-- Actual pointwise empirical force acting on the shared random optimiser
and random cloud. This is not an expectation over the sampling law. -/

/-- Actual pointwise sampler force in the same random coordinates. -/

/-- The lifted optimiser force is the original finite empirical average
almost everywhere, using the same optimiser realisation for every particle. -/

/-- Unpacking the lifted sampler force gives exactly the original force on
each particle, with the same shared random optimiser. -/

/-- Full cloud form of the same almost-everywhere sampler identification. -/

/-- The actual random empirical force satisfies exactly the force assumption
used by the M-MFPO and HOL Gaussian-coordinate error theorems. -/

/-- The actual random coordinatewise sampler force satisfies the other
primitive force assumption of both Gaussian-coordinate error theorems. -/

/-- Full raw force in encoded cloud coordinates. -/

/-- The complete coupled L² force is exactly the original raw force
samplewise, including the shared random optimiser. -/

/-- The force kick acts pointwise by the original empirical optimiser and
coordinatewise sampler forces. -/

/-- The entire OBABO update on L² coordinates is the original raw update
almost everywhere. No pointwise update-identification assumption is used. -/

/-- The complete HOL implementation, including the sequential random
parameter update and both original force lifts, acts by the raw update
almost everywhere. All four coordinates use the same sample. -/

end Random
end ParticleForceData
/-- Explicit Euclidean cloud encoding: a flattened `(particle, coordinate)`
array is curried into the paper's collection of particle vectors. -/

/-- The constructed encoding reads exactly the intended particle coordinate. -/

/-- Encoding inverse simply repacks the original particle coordinates. -/

end ParticleMomentumRate

import PBGSO.MomentumRates
import UnadjustedLangevin.ProductBrownian
import UnadjustedLangevin.GaussianInnovationVectors

/-! # Actual Gaussian/Brownian coupling for M-MFPO

Normalised Brownian increments on the half-step grid give exactly the
independent standard Gaussian innovations used by the proposed implementation.
Their L² radii and the noise-matching error are derived, with explicit spatial
dimension. Independence of coordinate grid paths is a visible hypothesis for
the joint standard-Gaussian law; it is not inferred from marginal Brownianity.
-/

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped NNReal ENNReal
namespace PBGSO.Methods

variable {Ω I : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [Fintype I]
  (Q : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]

/-- A genuine standard-Gaussian vector from each half Brownian interval. -/

/-- Every half-step innovation has the exact square-root-dimension L² norm. -/

/-- The entire innovation sequence has the iid standard multivariate
Gaussian law. In particular both halves and all iterations are independent. -/

/-- The implementation's net momentum innovation is coupled to the sum of
the two actual normalised Brownian half increments. The local discrepancy is
explicitly O(h sqrt(h)); no noise-error premise remains. -/

/-- The comparison increment is the actual scaled Brownian increment over
the two adjacent half intervals, coordinate by coordinate almost surely. -/

/-! # Actual Gaussian/Brownian coupling for M-MFPO

Normalised Brownian increments on the half-step grid give exactly the
independent standard Gaussian innovations used by the proposed implementation.
Their L² radii and the noise-matching error are derived, with explicit spatial
dimension. Independence of coordinate grid paths is a visible hypothesis for
the joint standard-Gaussian law; it is not inferred from marginal Brownianity.
-/

  (Q : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]

/-- A genuine standard-Gaussian vector from each half Brownian interval. -/

/-- Every half-step innovation has the exact square-root-dimension L² norm. -/

/-- The entire innovation sequence has the iid standard multivariate
Gaussian law. In particular both halves and all iterations are independent. -/

/-- The implementation's net momentum innovation is coupled to the sum of
the two actual normalised Brownian half increments. The local discrepancy is
explicitly O(h sqrt(h)); no noise-error premise remains. -/

/-- The comparison increment is the actual scaled Brownian increment over
the two adjacent half intervals, coordinate by coordinate almost surely. -/

end PBGSO.Methods

HOL-MYPGD: new verified quadrature bound

HOL-MYPGD first takes an Euler parameter step, then applies the appendix's affine three-coordinate sampler update. Let GGG be its sampler force, globally LLL-Lipschitz in position uniformly over the parameter, and let h≥0h\ge0h≥0. For the exact line force D=∫0hG(θ,x+tu)dtD=\int_0^hG(\theta,x+tu)dtD=∫0h​G(θ,x+tu)dt, Lean proves

∥D−hG(θ,x)∥≤12L∥u∥h2.\|D-hG(\theta,x)\|\le\tfrac12L\|u\|h^2.∥D−hG(θ,x)∥≤21​L∥u∥h2.

Keeping the same initial state and innovation triple, the full-state discrepancy between endpoint and line quadrature is bounded by

(h/2+1+∣μ31∣)12L∥u∥h2.\left(h/2+1+|\mu_{31}|\right)\tfrac12L\|u\|h^2.(h/2+1+∣μ31​∣)21​L∥u∥h2.

This is a new verified local quadrature bound for the actual implemented endpoint choice. The comparison method uses the same affine response and exact line quadrature; it is not the exact SDE. Covariance validity, an infinite-horizon rate and convergence to the original unsmoothed optimum are separate questions.

/-!
# HOL-MYPGD: the paper's endpoint quadrature and its verified error

The seven coefficients below are transcribed from Appendix `mmle_details.tex`.
The covariance law is deliberately not asserted by a pathwise definition. The
innovation argument contains a correlated triple for each particle; no noise is
added to the optimiser. The sampler force may be smoothed while the optimiser
uses the original force. Thus these results do not silently remove smoothing
bias or the finite-particle error.

/-- Seven scalar response coefficients of the higher-order implementation. -/

/-- The explicit coefficients in the paper. Meaningful physical parameters
have `α>0`, `h>0`; the pathwise map and bounds themselves use no division
cancellation and remain algebraically defined at zero. -/

/-- State `(θ,x,u,v)`, allowing `X` itself to be a finite particle cloud. -/

/-- The physically useful sum of the four coordinate discrepancies. -/

/-- Triangle inequality in the sum of the four coordinate errors. -/

/-- Affine sampler response to an integrated force `D` and a correlated triple
of innovations. This is exactly the three sampler rows in the appendix. -/

and the sampler force is evaluated at the updated parameter. -/

/-- Sensitivity to replacing the integrated force. All other data, including
the entire innovation triple, are identical. -/


/-- Sum of the three innovation discrepancies. -/

/-- The full affine response estimate, retaining the coefficient dependence. -/

/-- Explicit stability factor for the implemented higher-order map. -/

/-- New one-step stability bound for the actual endpoint implementation,
derived using the independent Lipschitz properties of `Fbar` and `G`.
The factor uses maximum column sums and tends to one as the step vanishes. -/

section Quadrature
variable [CompleteSpace X]

/-- The line-integrated force that the endpoint approximation replaces. -/

/-- New quadrature guarantee, proved by integrating Lipschitz variation along
the actual line segment. It is not an assumed numerical-error recurrence. -/

/-- New full-state local consistency bound for the implementation's endpoint
force quadrature versus the same affine Gaussian update with exact line
quadrature. It applies to every supplied innovation and every particle count.
This comparison is not an exact-SDE convergence claim. -/

/-- New finite-step bound for the endpoint-quadrature implementation against

HOL-MYPGD: finite-horizon integral-reference error

The finite-horizon HOL theorem compares the actual appendix-coefficient map with compatible segments of the original higher-order additive integral equations. Assume separate joint sum-norm Lipschitz constants LF,LG≥0L_F,L_G\ge0LF​,LG​≥0, h≥0h\ge0h≥0, an integrable reference drift with increment modulus at most CtC\sqrt tCt​, optimiser force bound FθF_\thetaFθ​, sampler force bound FGF_GFG​ evaluated at the Euler-updated parameter, and auxiliary norm bounds U,VU,VU,V. Let W=∣h∣/2+1+∣μ31∣W=|h|/2+1+|\mu_{31}|W=∣h∣/2+1+∣μ31​∣ and

AH=max⁡ ⁣{(1+∣h∣LF)(1+W∣h∣LG), ∣μ12∣+∣μ22∣+∣μ32∣, ∣μ13∣+∣μ23∣+∣μ33∣}.A_H=\max\!\left\{(1+|h|L_F)(1+W|h|L_G),\ |\mu_{12}|+|\mu_{22}|+|\mu_{32}|,\ |\mu_{13}|+|\mu_{23}|+|\mu_{33}|\right\}.AH​=max{(1+∣h∣LF​)(1+W∣h∣LG​), ∣μ12​∣+∣μ22​∣+∣μ32​∣, ∣μ13​∣+∣μ23​∣+∣μ33​∣}.

The verified deterministic coefficient and splitting budget is

DH=(h2/2+∣μ31h∣)FG+(∣μ12−h∣+∣μ22−1∣+∣μ32+γh∣)U+(∣μ13∣+∣μ23−γh∣+∣μ33−1+αh∣)V+h2LGFθ.\begin{aligned} D_H={}&(h^2/2+|\mu_{31}h|)F_G +(|\mu_{12}-h|+|\mu_{22}-1|+|\mu_{32}+\gamma h|)U\\ &+(|\mu_{13}|+|\mu_{23}-\gamma h|+|\mu_{33}-1+\alpha h|)V +h^2L_GF_\theta. \end{aligned}DH​=​(h2/2+∣μ31​h∣)FG​+(∣μ12​−h∣+∣μ22​−1∣+∣μ32​+γh∣)U+(∣μ13​∣+∣μ23​−γh∣+∣μ33​−1+αh∣)V+h2LG​Fθ​.​

The full-state sum-norm error satisfies

en≤AHne0+(DH+B+83Chh)∑j=0n−1AHj.e_n\le A_H^n e_0+\left(D_H+B+\tfrac83Ch\sqrt h\right)\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}A_H^j.en​≤AHn​e0​+(DH​+B+38​Chh​)j=0∑n−1​AHj​.

The map stability and local consistency inequalities are proved before this recurrence is summed. For a stochastic application, the moment/modulus bounds and the innovation/Brownian coupling must be instantiated. The supporting noise and covariance modules construct that coupling and identify the printed Gaussian law at positive physical parameters. The exact-budget bound alone does not assert a convergence order, uniform-in-time accuracy or a target-law bound; the next theorem adds the coefficient and noise estimates needed for a finite-horizon rate.

assumed implicitly. A finite-horizon result follows from the map stability and
this derived local consistency estimate.

continuous integral equation; this is not substituted for the implementation. -/

HOL-MYPGD: explicit square-root-step rate and constructed Gaussian coupling

The additional coefficient analysis gives an explicit finite-horizon square-root-step rate. Take α>0\alpha>0α>0, γ≥0\gamma\ge0γ≥0, 0<h≤10<h\le10<h≤1, and the nonnegative force, auxiliary and reference-modulus bounds from the preceding theorem. Let KHK_HKH​ be the computed stability constant and D0D_0D0​ the computed quadratic local consistency constant. If the local innovation discrepancy is at most CξhhC_\xi h\sqrt hCξ​hh​, the proved error estimate is

en≤eKHnh[e0+(D0+Cξ+83C)(nh)h].e_n\le e^{K_Hnh}\left[e_0+\left(D_0+C_\xi+\tfrac83C\right)(nh)\sqrt h\right].en​≤eKH​nh[e0​+(D0​+Cξ​+38​C)(nh)h​].

Here CξC_\xiCξ​ is a noise-coupling constant, distinct from the number of particles. The headline Gaussian-coordinate theorem substitutes its proved value directly, so it has no unknown noise-error premise. The coefficient remainders and AH≤1+KHhA_H\le1+K_HhAH​≤1+KH​h are derived from the exact printed formulas, rather than postulated.

The canonical HOL noise construction proves a correlated Gaussian response triple coupled to an actual Brownian increment, its Gram covariance and independent time/spatial blocks. The covariance module identifies all six expanded manuscript entries with that Gram matrix and proves positive semidefiniteness. Complete proof and source context

HOL Gaussian bounds on actual independent initial/noise particle spaces

Each actual particle seed pairs an initial sampler variable with an independent canonical Brownian source. Forgetting the initial states and flattening particle/spatial indices preserves the entire canonical noise source. The initial cloud has the exact iid marginal and is independent of that whole Brownian source, proved through their actual joint product law. The actual four-kernel HOL innovation array, including the coupled Brownian reference coordinate, therefore retains its full temporal/spatial joint law.

Isometric L2L^2L2 pullback preserves the explicit Gaussian coupling budget and the actual finite-horizon particle bound on this random-initial space. The generic pullback theorem displays its measure-preserving projection; ParticleNoiseSpace constructs that projection rather than assuming a final noise-law identity. Original integral-reference segments, coefficient signs, finite-horizon forces/velocities and square-root modulus remain explicit.

Complete proof and source context

Parameter-law compatibility proved for actual shared numerical packing

The full momentum state is packed into a shared Hilbert optimiser (θ,m)(\theta,m)(θ,m) and per-particle Hilbert sampler (x,v)(x,v)(x,v); HOL uses optimiser θ\thetaθ and nested Hilbert sampler (x,u,v)(x,u,v)(x,u,v). The full packed variables are square integrable, their pointwise identities are proved, and their actual paired-law parameter marginal equals the original phase θ\thetaθ law.

These are actual pushforward identities, with no final compatibility equality premise and no independence of interacting particles. The generic theorem also covers the actual parameter lift of a constructed L2L^2L2 interacting optimiser. Thus the numerical target-law premise is discharged when the same actual reference process and packing are used; identifying independently supplied numerical integral references with a different process construction remains a separate equation-level task.

Actual numerical parameter bounds to stationary and original targets

The actual particle method parameter errors now combine the explicitly proved Gaussian discretization budgets with the actual weak-process stationary parameter bound:

∥θ^nN,h−θ⋆∥L2≤Bdisc(h,n)+κe−ρnhd0+LΨρκVN(1−e−ρnh).\|\widehat\theta_{n}^{N,h}-\theta_\star\|_{L^2}\le B_{\rm disc}(h,n)+\sqrt\kappa e^{-\rho nh}d_0+\frac{L_\Psi}{\rho}\sqrt{\frac{\kappa V}{N}}(1-e^{-\rho nh}).∥θnN,h​−θ⋆​∥L2​≤Bdisc​(h,n)+κ​e−ρnhd0​+ρLΨ​​NκV​​(1−e−ρnh).

The budget BdiscB_{\rm disc}Bdisc​ is exactly the earlier M-MFPO or HOL finite-horizon square-root-step expression, including its initial error. The integral-reference packages contain the primitive force, Brownian, compatible integral-equation, finite-horizon moment and modulus contracts; the stationary-target package contains the weak-generator, frozen-target and all-initial-coupling realization data. Neither package contains the requested final error bound as a field.

Generic weak-process interface. Reference-law compatibility remains explicit in these intermediate statements. The numerical reference parameter law at time nh must equal the interacting optimiser parameter law used in the weak-process theorem. A proved pushforward identity and L2L^2L2 triangle transfer the reference bound; the code does not infer this law equality merely from the two separate solution descriptions.

For HOL, changing from its surrogate stationary target to the original zero-gradient target adds the proved bias Lε/mL\varepsilon/mLε/m. Its assumptions are an actual L2L^2L2 pair of original/surrogate target sampler variables within ε\varepsilonε, the original gradient expectation identity, zero surrogate mean observation, a spatial LLL-Lipschitz observation, and the displayed positive-mmm gradient monotonicity pairing. The Moreau-specific ε\varepsilonε and proper TV-prior repair are not proved. These are finite-horizon conditional bounds; they do not assert uniform-in-time numerical mixing.

Checked correction: the HOL coefficients are not the full exact linear flow

An exact force-free fundamental matrix would satisfy μ22′=γμ32\mu_{22}^\prime=\gamma\mu_{32}μ22′​=γμ32​. At α=γ=h=1\alpha=\gamma=h=1α=γ=h=1, Lean proves that the printed coefficients instead have mismatch 1−3e−1≠01-3e^{-1}\ne01−3e−1=0. This exact counterexample justifies retaining coefficient-error terms. It does not reject the numerical map or establish a replacement covariance law.

import PBGSO.HigherOrderMethod

/-! # A checked correction to the higher-order coefficient interpretation

The printed affine coefficients define a numerical method, but they are not
the exact matrix exponential of the force-free higher-order subsystem. For
alpha=gamma=1, a necessary fundamental-matrix identity would be
mu22'=mu32. At h=1 the two sides differ. This does not invalidate the
implementation or the proved numerical error budgets.
-/

Hybrid-target bias from a supplied original/surrogate coupling

If the original gradient is strongly monotone with positive constant mmm, its target star has zero gradient, the surrogate mean original observation vanishes at a, and an actual original/surrogate sampler coupling at a has L2L^2L2 radius ε\varepsilonε, a spatial LLL-Lipschitz observation gives distance at most Lε/mL\varepsilon/mLε/m. The proof compares the actual Bochner force expectations and applies the gradient residual bound. This does not assume or prove a Moreau coupling radius for the TV example.

import PBGSO.GeneralProcess

/-! # Bias caused by changing the sampler target

The hybrid HOL method observes the original force while sampling a smoothed
law. It need not have the original objective's critical point. Strong
monotonicity of the original gradient and an actual coupling of the original
and surrogate sampler laws give the explicit bias bound below. No smoothing
coupling bound or validity of the manuscript's TV prior is silently assumed.
-/

Complete proof and source context

Model and target conditions

Hybrid smoothing. HOL-MYPGD samples from πθλ∝e−Eλ\pi_\theta^\lambda\propto e^{-E^\lambda}πθλ​∝e−Eλ while observing the original F=∂θEF=\partial_\theta EF=∂θ​E. For finite λ\lambdaλ, the equilibrium force can be biased relative to the original objective. A bound to its critical point must include a force/smoothing bias estimate.

Printed HOL coefficients. The implemented affine coefficient matrix is not the exact full force-free linear flow: its printed coefficients fail μ22′=γμ32\mu_{22}'=\gamma\mu_{32}μ22′​=γμ32​ for positive α,γ,h\alpha,\gamma,hα,γ,h. The formal map uses those actual coefficients, with explicit consistency remainders. Its printed Gaussian covariance is identified with the response-kernel Gram matrix separately; this does not make the drift matrix the full exact flow.

TV model. Standard image total variation is unchanged by adding a constant image. Hence ∫Rde−eθTV(x)dx=∞\int_{\mathbb R^d}e^{-e^\theta\mathrm{TV}(x)}dx=\infty∫Rd​e−eθTV(x)dx=∞. The source's assumed finite prior normaliser requires a repaired domain, anchoring or coercive penalty; the displayed full-space prior does not satisfy it. Repair can change the normalisation derivative and dimension term.

Experimental claims. Neural EBM experiments do not establish global strong monotonicity, Lipschitz constants, the uniform variance bound or the hypocoercive friction threshold. The reported acceleration and reconstruction quality remain empirical observations. The source and formal-scope audit records these distinctions.

No grid-approximation or stochastic-isometry premise is supplied. These are deterministic coefficient-density facts, without an SDE existence assertion.

Clamping a deterministic grid at a cut and selecting its actual nonempty intervals gives a monotone finite split grid. The literal embedded step function is exactly the deterministic time restriction, with the corresponding interval and refinement identities proved.

Indicator-function columns embed finite left-step coefficients into the genuine L2L^2L2 time space. Disjoint interval inner products give the exact sum of interval lengths times coefficient norms squared. Arbitrary compatible subdivision preserves the embedded coefficient itself.

Lean checks the formal proofs. The default PBGSO verifier checks source hashes, every displayed declaration, exact assumption inventory, source-result coverage, local links and regeneration. Its successful run certifies documentation fidelity, not completion of all paper theorems. The strict --require-complete command rejects any open source-result, actual method-bound or required bridge obligation. Its source correspondence uses the documented SDE meaning of A2 and ordinary finite signed-work convention for the constant-diffusion source2 branch; an extended-negative-work theorem is not claimed. The audit file exposes logical axioms separately from analytic theorem premises. This source-based development has no proof PDF export.
